newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. to monitor EU wheat price link with SRW.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to monitor EU wheat price link with SRW.

text.p: The United States will continue to monitor European Union wheat export pricing in the light of its commitment not to undercut soft red winter prices, Agriculture Undersecretary Gene Moos said on Sunday.

"We are very interested in whether they stay with the spread with soft red winter because soft red is in tight supply in the United States and we expect it to stay firmer than other classes of wheat even though prices are weakening generally," Moos told Reuters during a visit to an international food fair.
The EU, under fire from Washington for restoring wheat export subsidies, has pledged not to sell beneath soft red wheat prices in an apparent effort to avert a subsidy spat.

The United States has hinted current EU refunds -- most recently 6.9 Ecus or $9 per tonne -- are not enough to spark a response but any move seen as challenging U.S. markets would summon a new wave of subsidised EEP export bonuses.
U.S. Agriculture Department General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait, travelling with Moos, said even the coupling of EU prices to soft red winter may seem like a discount on paper.
"Even using soft red as a basis is a bit of a discount theoretically, because the EU has historically sold somewhere between soft red and hard red winter prices," he said.

The last EU refund of a maximum 6.9 Ecus per tonne valued November French wheat at $165.31 a tonne when it was approved last Thursday, according to a Reuters calculation. Soft red winter was quoted at around $164 per tonne at the same time, but has since drifted towards $160 per tonne for November.
